newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin adviser supports Kulikov's aluminium probe.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin adviser supports Kulikov's aluminium probe.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's economic issues advisor, Mikhail Delyagin, defended on Tuesday comments made by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov about a probe into alleged crimes in the Russian aluminium sector.

"The reply of the deputy prime minister (Kulikov is also a cabinet member) to an open letter from the aluminium king Reuben corresponds completely to the spirit and letter of the president's address to parliament," Delyagin said in a written statement.
Yeltsin said last week in his annual state-of-the-nation address that the elimination of economic corruption was, among other things, key to an economic turnaround.
Yeltsin vowed to root out corruption and wage a ruthless fight against crime sweeping Russia.
Delyagin said order and fair competition were the main tasks for the Russian economy.
Kulikov is conducting an investigation into alleged crimes in the Russian aluminium sector.
The probe has upset London-based Trans-World Group, which has a giant presence in the sector through its equity stakes and tolling deals with smelters.

Kulikov, in an stinging letter to Trans-World executive chairman David Reuben, vowed on Tuesday to continue an investigation into the alleged crimes, which he said had given foreign firms an unfair advantage in the sector.
But he said that there was no question of confiscating property. --Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
